newsitem.title: USA: McDermott expects better year in fiscal 98.
newsitem.headline: McDermott expects better year in fiscal 98.

text.p: J. Ray McDermott SA said Friday it believes fiscal 1998 will be a better year than the year ended March 31 although some of the problems that led to 1997's loss still linger.

Revenues rose a bit last year -- to $1.37 billion from $1.23 billion in 1996. The company had a loss of $4.1 million in 1997 compared to earnings of 187,000 in 1996 and its loss per share following preferred dividends rose to $0.28 from $0.19 in fiscal 1996.
"J. Ray McDermott experienced a very difficult fiscal year," chief executive Roger Tetrault said.
"While the volume of activity exceeded fiscal 1996 levels, many projects carried low profit margins.
"Although certain of these projects will continue to dampen fiscal 1998 results, we believe that fiscal 1998 will be a better year than fiscal 1997.

"Our consolidated backlog was $1.8 billion at March 31, 1997 compared with $1.0 billion a year earlier. We also have experienced some improvement in pricing. As we continue to restructure these operations and focus on profitability, we are optimistic that we will see financial improvement."
As previously announced, J. Ray McDermott and its parent, McDermott International Inc, are conducting an internal investigation of allegations of wrongdoing by a limited number of former employees.

It said the allegations, if true, could result in civil and/or criminal liability for the company. At this time, the company does not have sufficient information to predict the ultimate outcome of this matter, it said.
